source.summary: GitHub Actions ‘Embedder footprint’ runs for PR #293 (branch fix/191-jit-direct-calls at head 764a453e568e6ed29855c6c0ca7f6eff1cd5a912 — branch commit f0015b9 (enter JIT callees directly on native-to-native calls (#191)), merge commit 159796d bringing in current main 41bca95 (PR #290, #190), and a formatting fix on top; ubuntu-24.04, Rust 1.96.0): workflow_dispatch runs 45320518752 and 45320533005 against the branch and pull-request run 45320509989, which built the same tree, produced byte-identical sizes for every gated series
source.derivation: Re-baseline for PR #293 (#191, JIT-to-JIT calls round-tripping through the runtime with a per-call mutex). Native-to-native calls now enter the compiled callee directly: after the ordinary frame preparation, the call helpers resolve the callee through the per-store entry table (the StoreInner funcaddr slots, upgraded from Weak) and enter it via enter_compiled_from_jit_call, falling back to the previous lazy-compile path on a miss. The per-call cache mutex touch is gone: recency lives in an AtomicU64 stamp on CompiledFunction, advanced on every direct call but only rewritten every 32 ticks. The TLS entry-depth counter (the 256 nested-entry cap) is removed; native recursion depth is bounded by the same value-stack accounting as interpreter recursion (#166, #126 limits). The branch was cut from main at b39b116 before PR #290 (#190) merged, so current main (41bca95) was merged in before measurement (merge commit 159796d); the merge combines #191's removal of the entry-depth thread-local with #190's move of the interpreter stop target into ExecuteContext, and both thread-locals are gone from the merged tree. Attribution was isolated by measuring current main alone (workflow_dispatch run 45320550102, gate success): it reproduces the previous baseline exactly on all 32 gated series, so every delta below is this PR's own. Only 8 of the 32 gated series change — the two configurations that link the JIT entry code. In release, core-jit grows by 1,152 B stripped file / 976 B stripped .text and core-aot shrinks by 560 B / 448 B. In release-size, core-jit grows by 272 B / 240 B and core-aot shrinks by 448 B / 304 B. Against the original #164 baseline, the largest cumulative growth remains the release component stripped file series, unchanged at +9.59% (2,433,656 B to 2,667,120 B). The core-aot configuration, added by PR #267 after the #164 baseline, is not part of the cumulative comparison. Run-to-run spread was again 0 B for every gated series across the three samples.
